qa.cite: Every new-state id is watched failing on the current tree.
qa.reply_head:
Yes
Every rule has an explicit red-first test path. The three scenarios map cleanly to failing tests on the current tree: whole-word scans on the eight tracked files, exit-code assertions for `--tree` and the hook, and multi-word account path rewrites S1 to S5. The test matrix rigorously pairs failing assertions with controls (B4, B6, T3, T4, G4, S6) to ensure violations are caught without false passes or overreach. audit lens.reply_head:
Yes
The proposal thoroughly addresses all three defects (leak, exit code, space rule) and establishes a robust, git-verifiable evidence chain. The acknowledged CI limitation for the local name is properly mitigated by local hooks and scans, with planted rows ensuring CI coverage. The rule-based scrub of records preserves integrity, and the red-first workflow with separate worktrees and fresh contexts maintains auditability. No loophole allows passing while breaking the practice.

decider.cite: independent gate reviewer and sign-off two further fresh Claude contexts
decider.reply_head:
Yes
The evaluation is framed rigorously around empirical verification. The characterisation tests (C1, R1) ensure no regressions, and new-state tests (376-1 through 376-3) separate code changes from blob rewrites with deterministic exit-code and whole-word gating. The task force contains every necessary seat with strict session segregation: read-only architecture, isolated worktrees for red and green, second review, an independent gate reviewer replaying red on the pre-change tree, and a final sign-off seat. Evidence requirements are thoroughly grounded in reproducible git state and blob hash verification. Note: ensure CI logs explicitly reco
